cards.text: David, king of Israel, and all Israel have brought the ark of God into the City of David with shouting, horns, harps and lyres (1 Chronicles 15:28-29). They place it inside the tent David pitched for it. Then they present burnt offerings and peace offerings before God.

cards.question: David finishes the burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then what does he do?

answers.text: He blesses the people in the name of the LORD
He reads the Law of Moses to the people
He leads the people on a march through the city

cards.text: Then David starts handing out food: a loaf of bread, a date cake and a raisin cake. Three treats and not ONE cookie, but I'm not upset, friend, I'm just saying it out loud.

cards.question: David hands out the bread, date cake and raisin cake only to the Levites who carried the ark.

cards.text: Next, David appoints some of the Levites, the ones the LORD chose to carry the ark (1 Chronicles 15:2), to minister before the ark of the LORD. Part of the job is to CELEBRATE, friend, so somebody put THAT on my apron.

cards.question: David appoints some Levites to minister before the ark: to celebrate, to give ___ and to praise the LORD, the God of Israel.

cards.text: Asaph, one of the Levite singers (1 Chronicles 15:16-17), is the chief, with a whole crew under him on harps and lyres while he sounds the cymbals. The priests Benaiah and Jahaziel blow the trumpets regularly before the ark.

On that day David first commits to Asaph and his associates a song of thanksgiving to the LORD. It opens with a call: give thanks to the LORD, call on His name and make known His deeds among the nations.
Then it keeps going: sing to Him, sing praises to Him, tell of all His wonders and glory in His holy name. That's four things to do, friend, and I can't get TWO done before my oven timer goes off.

cards.question: David's song calls on the hearts of those who seek the LORD to rejoice.

cards.text: Then the song says to seek out the LORD and His strength, seek His face always, and remember the wonders He has done, His marvels and the judgments He has pronounced. Friend, I walk across my bakery to the oven and forget why I came, and my WHOLE planet is one bakery.

cards.question: This part of David's song calls people to seek the LORD and remember His wonders. Who does it call?
David's song says the LORD's judgments reach only as far as Israel.

cards.text: Next the song says to remember His covenant forever, the word He ordained for a thousand generations. It's the covenant He made with Abraham, the forefather of God's people, the oath He swore to Abraham's son Isaac, confirmed to Isaac's son Jacob as an everlasting covenant.

cards.question: David's song says God made a covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. What does God say He will give them?

cards.text: But back when they were few in number, few indeed, and strangers in the land, they wandered from nation to nation. Few INDEED, friend, that's not a nation, that's a group chat.

cards.question: While Israel's forefathers wander from one kingdom to another, what does the LORD do?

answers.text: He lets no one oppress them
He lets them fend for themselves
He sends them into the desert

cards.question: The LORD lets no one oppress the wanderers. He rebukes ___ on their behalf: “Do not touch My anointed ones! Do no harm to My prophets!”

cards.text: Now David's song turns to the whole world: sing to the LORD, all the earth, and proclaim His salvation day after day. Declare His glory among the nations, His wonders among ALL peoples.

cards.question: David's song says the LORD is to be feared above all gods. What reason does it give?

answers.text: Other gods are idols but He made the heavens
Other gods are new but He was there first
Other gods are far but He is close by

cards.text: Then the song says, “Splendor and majesty are before Him; strength and joy fill His dwelling.”

cards.question: David's song calls only on the people of Israel to ascribe glory and strength to the LORD.

cards.text: Ascribe to the LORD the glory due His name, the song goes on, and come before Him. Worship the LORD in the splendor of His holiness.

cards.question: When the families of the nations come before the LORD, what does David's song tell them to bring?

cards.text: The song says all the earth should tremble before Him, and the world is firmly established and cannot be moved.
Then the song says: let the heavens be glad and the earth rejoice, and let them say among the nations, “The LORD reigns!” Let the sea resound, and the fields exult too.

cards.question: In David's song, the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD too. What reason does the song give?

answers.text: He is coming to judge the earth
The long winter is finally over
The harvest has all come in

cards.text: Then the song circles right back to where it started: give thanks to the LORD.

cards.question: This time, David's song says to give thanks to the LORD because He is good and His loving devotion endures forever.
Then David's song gives the people a cry to God: save us, gather us and deliver us from the nations. What reason does the cry give?

answers.text: So they may give thanks to His holy name
So they may rule over every nation
So they may build Him a great temple

cards.text: And the song closes: “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting.”

cards.question: When David's song of thanksgiving ends, all the people answer with Amen and Praise the LORD.

cards.text: So David leaves Asaph and his associates before the ark to minister there regularly, along with Obed-edom and his sixty-eight relatives. Sixty-eight relatives on one job, friend, and my whole staff is me and a mustache. David also leaves Zadok the priest and his fellow priests before the tabernacle of the LORD at the high place in Gibeon, presenting burnt offerings morning and evening according to all that was written in the Law of the LORD. With them are Heman, Jeduthun and the rest chosen to give thanks to the LORD, with trumpets and cymbals for the music.

cards.question: Then all the people depart for their homes, and David returns home to ___ his household.
